relationships.subject: Capsaicin
relationships.evidence_quote: Capsaicin selectively activates the transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1), which is enriched in nociceptive primary afferents

relationships.subject: Capsaicin
relationships.evidence_quote: high concentrations of capsaicin lead to long-term defunctionalization mediated by the ablation of TRPV1-expressing afferent terminals

relationships.subject: Calpain
relationships.evidence_quote: Recent studies have shown that capsaicin-induced Ca2+/calpain-mediated ablation of axonal terminals is necessary to produce long-lasting analgesia in a mouse model of neuropathic pain.

key_findings: High-dose capsaicin causes TRPV1/Ca2+/calpain-mediated ablation of afferent terminals, giving months-long analgesia; low doses cause only reversible defunctionalization.
The 8% capsaicin patch is approved for PHN and diabetic neuropathy; injectable forms are in development.
